verdict.summary: Tenable is improving profitability faster than it is growing, making the stock a margin-execution case rather than a cyber momentum proxy. Q2 2026 revenue was $268.5M, up 8.6%, while GAAP operating margin improved to 4.6% from negative 3.0% and non-GAAP margin reached 24.7%. Unlevered free cash flow was $45.3M, and FY2026 guidance calls for $1.075B-$1.081B revenue with $289M-$295M unlevered FCF. Tenable One, Hexa and AI Exposure can monetize a broader machine and cloud attack surface, yet growth trails larger platforms. The dated framework is 3.8x guided revenue and a 7.1% guided unlevered-FCF yield. A completed 15-minute close above $37.88 activates the plan; $34.52 is the Aug. 6 stop, with July highs at $42.9399 and $43.6699. A return to losses or weak platform additions invalidates the rerating.

business.overview:
Tenable sells subscriptions for vulnerability management, cloud exposure, identity exposure, operational technology security and the Tenable One exposure-management platform. Revenue grows through customer additions, platform conversion, asset coverage and renewal. Q2 added 381 enterprise platform customers and 32 net new six-figure customers.

The AI transmission channel is attack-surface complexity. More cloud assets, identities, agents and generated code create vulnerabilities that Tenable can discover, prioritize and remediate through Tenable One, Hexa and AI Exposure. The economic proof is platform-customer growth and cash conversion, not partnership announcements.

The model breaks if exposure management remains a feature rather than a budget category, or if platform consolidation favors larger endpoint and network vendors. Revenue growth of 8.6% leaves limited cushion for sales disruption. Tenable must preserve gross margin, sustain positive GAAP operating income and convert simplified packaging into larger contracts; otherwise the margin improvement becomes cost cutting around a structurally slow top line.
business.moat: Tenable's vulnerability data, asset coverage and installed scanning workflows create switching friction, while Tenable One can unify exposures across IT, cloud, identity and OT. The moat is narrower than a full security platform and must be defended through prioritization accuracy and workflow integration.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 revenue was $268.5M (+8.6%). GAAP operating income was $12.4M and margin 4.6%, versus a 3.0% loss margin a year earlier; non-GAAP operating margin was 24.7%. GAAP/non-GAAP diluted EPS were $0.03/$0.51, and unlevered FCF was $45.3M. Q3 revenue guidance is $270M-$273M; FY2026 guidance is $1.075B-$1.081B with $289M-$295M unlevered FCF. Caveat: adjusted margins exclude recurring equity compensation and growth remains single-digit. Tenable must deliver $289M-$295M unlevered free cash flow while restoring faster platform growth.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Tenable reported 110,139,983 shares outstanding on July 31, 2026 and 113,768,000 diluted weighted-average shares for Q2. The latter is the minimum calculable denominator; a current theoretical fully diluted count is unavailable because the filing does not reconcile all unvested and anti-dilutive awards. Tenable carries approximately $298M cash against $422M debt. Q2 repurchases of 5.2M shares for $100M reduce dilution only if they exceed employee issuance. No ATM or prospectus supplement was reviewed; buyback efficiency and debt service, not emergency equity financing, are the capital tests.
